bio: I am a money coach. Not a financial advisor who manages your investments, not an accountant who files your return: the person who sits on your side of the table, opens your numbers with you, and works through them until you can see the whole year and the next twenty.

The families I work with look like mine. Several children in day school, a shul we walk to, camp in the summer, a bar mitzvah on the calendar and a wedding somewhere past it. The general advice does not fit us. A budget app has no line for tuition assistance or Pesach. I built the free tools on this site because I could not find one that did.

squeeze.title: The squeeze no general planner sees

lines.label: Tuition
lines.text: The largest line in the house, for every child, for twenty years. It arrives before retirement saving has had its turn.

lines.label: The year
lines.text: Dues in Elul, nine yom tov meals in Tishrei, Pesach in Nisan, camp in June. A Jewish year spends in spikes, and the spikes land on the same months every year.

lines.label: The simchas
lines.text: A bar mitzvah at thirteen, a year in Israel at eighteen, a wedding in the twenties. Each one is on the calendar today, and each one is paid for in a single year.

lines.label: The house
lines.text: It has to be within a walk of the shul, inside the eruv. The streets that qualify carry a premium, and the mortgage page never asks about tuition.

steps.title: A free call
steps.text: Twenty minutes. You tell me what is keeping you up; I tell you whether I can help and what it would look like. No numbers needed yet.

steps.title: The first sessions
steps.text: We go stop by stop down one path: the big picture, income, spending, debt, the cushion, what you own, taxes, the goals with dates, and the big decisions. I type as we talk; the picture updates in front of you.

steps.title: Homework and a recap
steps.text: Every session ends with a recap you keep: what changed, what is next, and two or three pieces of homework with dates. Find the 401(k) fee. Call the tuition committee. Price the camp.

steps.title: Monthly check-ins
steps.text: Between sessions, a two-minute check-in once a month: what moved, how you feel about money on a scale of one to five, homework ticked. We see the progress photo, not just the snapshot.

whoFor.title: Who this is for
yes: Two earners, or one, with children in day school or about to be
A household that feels squeezed on an income that should not feel squeezed
A family with a simcha or a house on the horizon and no plan for it yet
Anyone who has tried a budgeting app and given up because it had no line for tuition
no: Anyone looking for investment picks or someone to manage a portfolio
A halachic ruling on maaser or inheritance: I will do the arithmetic and send you to your rav with a number

faq.a: No. I do not sell products, manage money or pick investments. I coach: we work your own numbers together and you make the decisions. For a ruling, a return or a portfolio you keep your rav, your preparer and your advisor.

faq.q: Do I have to share my numbers before the call?
faq.a: No. The free call is a conversation. Numbers come in the first session, and we enter them together.
In the session, on my screen, in a file sealed with a passphrase that stays on my device. The free tools on this site keep everything in your own browser; nothing is sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do you work with families outside my community?
faq.a: Yes. Sessions are on a video call. The tools carry typical figures for the New York and New Jersey metro, the other large communities, and smaller ones.

faq.q: What if we cannot afford coaching right now?
faq.a: Use the free tools. Every page works on its own and none of it asks for an account. If the picture says something gives, the guide page says who to talk to, starting with the tuition committee and the shul.
